title: Post the journal to the ledger
goal: Post each journal line to the correct account and calculate a reliable ending balance.

slides.title: The journal tells the event; the ledger tells the account

items.heading: Ledger
items.text: What happened to Cash across all dates?

slides.takeaway: Posting reorganizes the same entries by account.
slides.notes: Do not create new transactions when posting. References support tracing in both directions.

slides.title: Read a T-account and a running-balance account
slides.takeaway: The ending balance is the difference between the sides.
slides.notes: A running-balance ledger shows the balance after each dated entry.

slides.title: Post dates, references, debits, and credits
slides.takeaway: Copy each amount to the same side as the journal entry.
slides.notes: Use exact account names. Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable are different accounts.

slides.title: Calculate a cash account balance
slides.notes: Excerpt through June 12. After all 16 transactions, Cash is $8,840.

slides.title: Calculate a payable with a credit balance
slides.takeaway: Usual payable: prior credit balance + credits − debits.
slides.notes: A signed-balance formula can work for all accounts if its convention is consistent.

slides.title: Post the same transaction to every affected account
slides.notes: Only T06 is displayed here; these are not complete June ledger accounts.

slides.title: Connect the course worksheet to ledger accounts

items.heading: Ending balance
items.text: Net the debit and credit totals.

slides.takeaway: The worksheet layout can change; the accounting logic stays.
slides.notes: Link or aggregate journal data rather than retyping it. If using SUMIFS, use exact account names and complete ranges.

slides.title: Try it: locate a missed or misposted line
slides.lead: What happens to Cash and the trial balance?
slides.takeaway: Repair the missing posting; do not invent a balancing entry.
slides.notes: The journal entry is already correct. This is a posting correction, not an adjusting entry.

items: Total debit balances are $1,800 too low.
Post the missing Cash debit with reference T05.

slides.title: Reconcile posting completeness to the journal

items: Every journal line appears in its ledger account.
Ending balances use a consistent sign convention.

slides.lead: Exit check: does posting change an entry’s accounts or amounts?
slides.notes: Supports the general ledger milestone. Matching movement totals alone cannot establish correct classification.

blocks.text: No. Posting transfers existing account effects to the ledger. It does not recognize the transaction again.
